newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian refiners lock in healthy forward margins.
newsitem.headline: Asian refiners lock in healthy forward margins.

text.p: Asian refiners enjoying their best margins in over a year are hedging their positions in the forward swaps market to lock in the high profits, industry sources said on Thursday.
"We have seen some refiners locking in their third and fourth quarter margins earlier this month," one broker said.

The refiners' good fortune was due to an unusually large spate of diesel and jet fuel purchases by two related local trading firms who in just over a month bought more than 12 million barrels of the two oil products.
Refiners in Singapore mainly refine Middle East crudes such as Arab Light and Dubai as well as regional grades such as Tapis.
A refining source said that currently the third quarter gas oil/Dubai crack spread was valued at about $7.30 per barrel, compared to the past four-year average of $6.20.
The nearer month crack spreads are much higher with the April spread currently valued at about $10.00, May at $8.90 and June at $8.00, sources said.
The spreads average out to $9.00 per barrel for the second quarter but refiners are not likely to have locked in their profits at such high levels as such hedging is done well forward.
So refiners were probably hedging their second quarter margins sometime in January or earlier, at which time spreads were about $2.00-3.00 less, sources said.
"Refiners would love to lock in their second quarter costs now, but chances are they can't as they would have done this long ago," the refining source said.
